issues.detail: Mostly covers the happy path; the rate limiter has no tests or error handling, and the instructions skip common failure scenarios such as GenServer call timeouts, restart-intensity limits, and Ecto changeset error handling.

scenarios.name: crash-safe-rate-limiter-genserver
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: a GenServer with start_link and check_rate, handle_call returning :ok or {:error, :rate_limited} over a 60s window, Process.send_after with a self-rescheduling handle_info(:cleanup), and the module added to the supervisor's children with :one_for_one. A uses ETS with a `check/1` function that doesn't go through handle_call, returns different tuples, and names its callback :sweep instead of :cleanup, so it misses several specific rubric items even though it is well designed and has the supervisor wiring.

scenarios.name: liveview-realtime-orders-dashboard
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric directly, with a {:new_order, order} broadcast and a handler that updates assigns with update/3. B has the connected? guard, :tick, ~H and a broadcast after insert, but it uses {:order_created, id} and re-queries instead of handling {:new_order, order}, which misses a specific rubric requirement.

scenarios.name: ecto-registration-with-safe-input
scenarios.rationale: B covers all rubric items (changeset piped to Repo.insert, {:ok}/{:error} case handling, explicit avoidance of String.to_atom, and `mix phx.new --database sqlite3` followed by `mix setup`), while A is strong on changeset and Ecto.Enum safety but omits `mix setup` (uses ecto.create/migrate instead) and never explicitly mentions String.to_atom.
